fragments.text: Hello, my name is Daniel Sikazue, I'm talking about artificial intelligence and how it helps in journalism to help citizens to attain their right to know. And so in this presentation, I will be talking about what the right to know is and how artificial intelligence is important in helping citizens and media in particular to help the citizens to demand that they should know. So first of all, I would like to say that the right to know is an epistemic right. The right to know is part of a broad range of epistemic rights, rights to goods like information, knowledge and the truth. in every society people desire to have information, to have knowledge and to have

the truth. These rights play a prominent role in our information-centric society but they often go unnoticed, they're disregarded and unprotected by governments and sometimes by commercial interests and it could also be by religious interests. And because of that those who control what citizens should know or what they think their citizens should know can exert a huge influence on the lives of the citizens and this becomes very dangerous in a democracy. Epistemic rights, when violated, can lead to harm on the lives of citizens, on the relationships that citizens form among themselves, between themselves and most in power between the citizens, and the greater global world, and the harm could extend to social and political institutions and communities. There are a lot of stumbling

blocks to the right to know. What do we mean by stumbling blocks? We are talking about the difficulties that citizens can encounter in wanting to exercise their right to know. So how citizens meaningfully express their voice about what the government is doing can only be possible if the people know what the government is doing. What this simply means is that it is impossible for citizens to know what the government is doing unless they know what the government is doing. In many countries, it is very difficult and almost impossible for citizens to know what the government is doing because of the existence of laws that are commonly known as official secrets acts. And these are the kind of laws that empower politicians to be able to decide what citizens

can know and what they cannot know because these politicians think citizens must not know everything. Where these official secrets are exists there is no free press and we know that a free press with little or no information about what the government is doing cannot provide an effective check on on government. It is the responsibility of the press to ensure that citizens know what the government is doing. Now, these official secrets arts can be quite excessive in some governments. Excessive secrecy has a corrosive effect on virtually all aspects of society and governance by undermining the quality of public decision making and preventing citizens from checking the abuses of public power. Societies, however, do not have to tolerate

excessive secrecy from their governments. Therefore, this means there is always a struggle between those wanting exercise their right to know and those who are preventing citizens from knowing what they should know. The right to know stretches beyond government. What this means is that the right to know cannot only be exercised when citizens want to know what the government was to do. It goes beyond knowing what the government is doing. There are intergovernmental organizations like the World Bank and the International Monetary Fund or the IMF that have today adopted and they do emphasize there must be policies, there must be regulations, there must be laws of full disclosure among the governments, among the institutions that they deal with.

There are also hundreds of major multinational corporations that have today adopted voluntary courts that require them to disclose a wide range of information about their environmental, labor, and other practices. It is Therefore, the right of citizens to demand and exercise their right to know which helps them to be able to make demands not only of corrupt governments or governments or institutions that are doing the wrong thing. Citizens have the power, or they have the right rather, to demand even from the cleanest, the best, the most honest of governments. they need to demand to know what these leaders are doing. However clean, however honest, however good, however legal, however clean the government might be, when citizens exercise the right to know they help this government to be able to get feedback about how the government is doing,

What this simply means is that any good person doing the right thing must know what citizens think about what they're doing. This way these good people, the honest people, the legal people, the people are doing everything according to the law are able to understand what people think, how people would want things to be done for them to improve on the way they're doing things. This in the long run leads to good policies, good laws, good rules, good development that is not only in the interest of the political leadership but in the interest of the general citizenry. There is a huge disconnect and inequalities we know between the developing countries and the developed countries.

And these inequalities are brought about by globalization. When citizens politicize their right to know, they can easily bridge that gap. In other words, think about a country like Zambia where we get a lot of loans. At the moment, we are getting medicines that are coming from the UK, from the US, from China. Citizens have the right to know who are the manufacturers of these medicines, what are the contents of these medicines, Under what conditions are these medicines given? Are these medicines given to citizens in those countries? How much money is being spent? What will be the short term and the long term effects of these medicines? When it comes to loans that are given to the Zambian government and African governments,

citizens need to know what are the conditions under which these loans are given? how well the acquisition of these loans impact national development, community development, and maybe the development of Africa as a whole. Without this information, the leaders can go to town to do whatever they want. It is therefore important that the citizens exercise their right to know. All over the world there is now a raging battle between two polar competing powers those that are asking for great transparency exercising the right to know and those that keep on insisting that what government does is purely the business of government and therefore they insist on privacy they insist on the confidentiality of these documents, they insist on evoking national

security laws, but this is not good at all. Now, where does artificial intelligence come in? Artificial intelligence tools can help to break down these, shall we say, provisions, or in short, artificial intelligence will help citizens to be able to get the kind of information that is kept as confidential, the information that is kept secret, the information that is kept under wraps, the information that goes in power who would not want to give this information because of wrongdoing, because of incompetence, because of just not knowing what they're doing. So using several different artificial intelligence tools, people are able to get this information. Now, I'd like to quote the New York Times in 2020, the New York Times 2020 Group Report

of January 2017. We said, we have not yet created a news report that takes full advantage of all the storytelling tools at our disposal and in the process does the best possible job of speaking to our potential audience. We have not yet created a news report that takes full advantage of all the storytelling tools at our disposal and in the process does the best possible job of speaking to our potential audience. End of court. What this simply means is, despite the existence of several artificial intelligence tools at At the moment, most media institutions are limited by the fact that they cannot use all the artificial intelligence tools, that sometimes some of these tools might actually be quite

expensive or maybe the combination in terms of use of these artificial intelligence tools can also be limiting. So using several tools, using several tools of artificial intelligence, journalists can help empower citizens to actively participate as both producers and consumers of the news, therefore helping the citizens to be more active participants in the democratic dispensation where the truth can be bled by misinformation and disinformation produced and perpetuated by those in power. Artificial intelligence helps journalists to live up to their modern role and this role is that of being facilitators of a process where citizens are able to navigate their way out of a maze of information and make sense of the information. What this simply means is that in today's journalism there are many sources, there is a lot of data dumping

and therefore citizens can become even more confused by the avalanche of information that they expose to. Using several artificial intelligence tools, journalists can get this information, process it and make it easier for citizens to be able to get this information. The existence of algorithms which are ubiquitous, when applied in a broad range of areas like commerce, the stock exchange, insurance businesses, social media, security surveillance, politics, education science, logistics and traffic, can actually help the citizens to get more information. Digital apps and services can be of value for news organizations, especially when these artificial intelligence tools help the journalists to be able to tell the story using text, images, video and the combination of these different applications.

Not only do they offer technology, they also offer extremely large distribution networks networks, or communities, or followers. In addition, the new storytelling tools described many more tools like Google AMP, Instagram, podcasts, Slack, and many others. This can help the media to be able to get information and to tell the story in a way that is easy to understand. Artificial intelligence is important in creating. Artificial intelligence is important in creating a truly free press, not defined by the press being homogeneous or the same, but diverse. Therefore, what for example, what media organization can decide not to publish based on the media institutions editorial and production guidelines, are the media institutions, given access to the same information, can publish this kind of information.

The democratization of the broadband puts pressure on legacy or traditional media to raise the standard of verification through the application of fact-checking tools. The internet can also enable journalists to sidestep, or not journalists but citizens, the internet can enable citizens to sidestep laws that might be in place that control access to information, especially in advertising or during times of elections. using social media can allow political material to be made available to millions targeted much more effectively than traditional media can ever manage. Now, ordinary citizens don't want to be distracted by irrelevant information. They don't want old or irrelevant information to to clutter up their timelines or search results. Having complete and accurate information, as required for historical archives, could

be a distraction and a disadvantage. It could stop them finding what they want to find. At Fish Intelligence helps meet citizens' information demands. Citizens want access to politically relevant information through as neutral and objective means as possible. They want not to be misled or manipulated by those who seek to influence their opinions or votes. Artificial intelligence can help journalists to get at the truth of what people in the news really know and do thereby avoiding the pitfall of reporting only what be seen. The Internet, we know, is not a permanent, perfect archive of historical material indexed by neutral and purely algorithmic services such as Google or access through neutral and apolitical platforms like Facebook. It is messy, dynamic and constantly changing.

Things have been deleted, modified and blocked all the time. Such engines, social media platforms and other services are not neutral public services but money-making self-serving businesses. Therefore, it is important that citizens are educated on some of the tools of artificial intelligence that exists. Artificial intelligence can help to check the veracity of records. To be more precise, an information resource useful for historical research can often be complex with notes, qualifications, references, and cross-references. It can need time, attention, and expertise to understand and to navigate through, but the complexity is necessary for the archive to be used. People trying to find the information without sufficient time, energy, and expertise may not find it. This is one of the reasons that Italy tools like search engines have become so popular.

They make it easy and fast to find things for everyone. People want to find the most relevant information quickly and don't want to be bothered with detailed fact checking or even know how to do proper fact or source checking. One of the reasons behind the fact use problems for most people if they require information exists but it is hard to find or if you take too much or too long to find or if it is obscured by morass of other information or if such information wanting to verify it becomes very difficult to find then for most practical purposes it might as well not exist, people trying to find the information without sufficient time, energy, and expertise

will find it very difficult. Atficient intelligence then becomes very useful here. Understanding the context, the complexity, the nuances, the dynamism, and the relationships between the various issues, and in particular, understanding the greatness of the whole situation can help citizens to take a more balanced view of each of the issues in 10. It is therefore important that journalists use artificial intelligence to get information that might be hidden, information that might be hard to find, but artificial intelligence also helps journalists to be able to interpret very quickly what this information is. It is therefore important that journalists know these tools and use them to be able to arrive at the truth and to help citizens to be able to get this information.
